supporting_observations.claim: During the alert period, WS-LMARTINS-01 made repeated connections to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080. The available Zeek records show connections at 13:30:58, 13:40:51, 13:43:21, 13:45:21, 13:50:28, 13:55:32, 14:00:10, 14:05:36, and 14:10:35 UTC.

At 14:10:35 UTC, the proxy logged a successful CONNECT tunnel from WS-LMARTINS-01 to updates.pixelforge-suite.com:443; the corresponding outbound connection was made by C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe. This matches the approved PixelForge updater service and its inventoried update domain.

The available records establish the approved updater as the source of the 14:10:35 connection, but do not identify the process or destination for the earlier proxy connections. The earlier connections could be consistent with the approved updater, but that is not established.

WS-LMARTINS-01 also made SMB connections to FILE-NWD-01 at 13:55:37 and 14:03:22 UTC; the corresponding FILE-NWD-01 logons identify ANONYMOUS LOGON. The available records do not establish what shares or resources were accessed or why.
At 14:11:03 UTC, DC-NWD-01 connected to WS-LMARTINS-01 on TCP port 135; a WmiPrvSE.exe process then ended on the workstation. These records do not establish the purpose of that activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: Sensor-status metadata reports a collection outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC for WS-LMARTINS-01 winsec and Sysmon, and for the proxy sensor. This leaves endpoint process attribution and proxy CONNECT details unavailable for much of the alert interval; the supplied metadata has no record ID.

Zeek connection records are available, but the earlier listed connections identify only the internal proxy endpoint and do not provide the external CONNECT host or process. No corresponding Zeek SSL records are included in the supplied evidence.

Obtain proxy CONNECT/access logs for 13:20–14:20 UTC, including destinations, users, request details, and tunnel metadata.
Obtain TLS/SSL metadata or other destination evidence for the connections, and verify the updater binary's signature, hash, and update activity.
